biotools.summary: Planum is an atlas of the human brain that runs in the browser. It is built from MRI data, so the surface, the sections and the white-matter tracts belong to the same brain and agree with one another. Widely used cortical parcellations, such as Destrieux, HCP-MMP and Julich-Brain, and a histological atlas of the deep structures are drawn on that anatomy, showing how differently they divide the same tissue. Selecting a region brings up what has been reported about it in meta-analyses of the imaging literature, lesion studies, intracranial stimulation and large group comparisons, each with its source. Guided tours follow the main pathways step by step, and every view is a link that can go into a lecture, a draft or a message to a colleague. A coordinate or a statistical map from a study can be placed on the brain to see where it falls, and a standard MNI template can replace the individual. Planum is free, needs no account, and is meant for learning and research, not for clinical use.

function.note: Draws MNI-space NIfTI-1 maps and coordinates on the atlas brain, its cut faces and its T1-weighted scan.
